about: The keyed facts the media watch times the press against: for each, the primary source's time and where that time comes from (primary_label says whether that time is a fact, read from the body itself, or only evidence: the earliest report), and the pattern (a regular expression over titles; for live-blog entries, over the entry's title) that says an item is about it. Ids are permanent. Kept by incident.media@web-summit.dinis; the primary times are the timeline's (incident.conductor@) and the meteorologist's. Titles only, except where match_entry_text is true.

facts.what: IPMA's red wind warning for Wednesday
facts.primary_note: IPMA's own issue time in its CAP message (data/weather/cap.json, incident.meteorologist@); the press said "divulgada às 08h31"

facts.what: The government's alert situation: schools and non-essential public services closed on Wednesday
facts.primary_note: portugal.gov.pt's page is dated 12:10; the minister announced it in the morning, so the press is ahead of the page
facts.pattern: escolas e servi[cç]os p[úu]blicos|situa[cç][aã]o de alerta|closes schools|escolas(?! (na|da) madeira)[^:]*(encerrad|fecha)[^:]*quarta|declara[^.]{0,30}situa

facts.what: Lisbon's mayor: everything indicates Web Summit cannot run on Wednesday
facts.primary_note: a spoken statement; no primary page found. The time is approximate: the first report is the earliest evidence of it
facts.pattern: web summit[^.]{0,80}(d[úu]vida|dever[áa] fechar|fechada|n[aã]o poder[áa])|(moedas|autarquia|autarca|c[âa]mara)[^.]{0,200}web summit|tudo indica[^.]{0,80}web summit

facts.what: The government recommends suspending Web Summit on Wednesday
facts.primary_note: no government page found; 17:53 is the first report (Jornal de Negócios' live blog, in the timeline)
Web Summit's "Important event update" page, published 19:09 (page data)

facts.what: IPMA moves Lisbon's red rain warning three hours earlier, to Wednesday 09:00
facts.primary_note: IPMA's CAP message sent 21:23 (data/weather/cap.json); its open-data feed showed it from the 23:51 read
notes: Outside the press: VOST Portugal (a volunteers' association, not an authority and not press) relayed the change on Bluesky at 22:20, 57 minutes after IPMA sent it (found by incident.social@: research/social/posts/2026-11-10.json, bsky-vost.pt-3mzyhxvwhry25). The finding for the press stands: no article title or live entry we could read reported it.

facts.what: The storm's track is further south than forecast (strongest winds south of Lisbon)
facts.primary_note: primary time unknown: IPMA's own channels had not changed when incident.conductor@ read them at 00:29 UTC on 11 November; every report rests on what IPMA told broadcasters
facts.pattern: trajec?t[óo]ria|mais (a|para) sul|a sul de lisboa|further south

quoted.attribution_as_printed: the latest runs of the ECMWF model (entry between Setúbal and Sines): models, not IPMA; nobody quoted
"IPMA" in the title; the bulletin is audio and was not listened to, so who speaks is not recorded

quoted.item: live blog entry, 22:35:24 (time from the page's own data; confirmed at incident.conductor@'s request)
quoted.attribution_as_printed: "O IPMA já admite"; a meteorologist of IPMA, in statements to Rádio Observador: entry between the Lisbon region and Cabo de São Vicente. The earliest text we read that attributes the shift to IPMA through a named role
"O IPMA já admite": the institute, no person or role named. Its opening sentence is word for word that of Observador's 22:35 entry

quoted.item: live page entry, about 23:15 (printed as "41 minutes ago" at our 23:55:58 read; the page gives no clock time)
quoted.attribution_as_printed: "the latest information from IPMA, released by RTP Notícias": relayed from RTP, no person or role named
the same meteorologist of IPMA, in statements to Rádio Observador

notes: VOST Portugal (a volunteers' association, not an authority) posted at 23:00 that the ECMWF model's 22:30 run showed the track shifting south: a model, not IPMA (in coverage.json, social.accounts).

On the wind: Observador's 22:35 entry and RTP's 23:08 entry say that if very strong winds form they would be felt south of Lisbon. Two later headlines speak of less wind: Expresso, 23:54 ("muda trajetória para sul, com menos vento") and CNN Portugal, 00:31 (the storm reaches Lisbon "com menos intensidade"). Headlines are evidence of what the press reports, not of the weather: IPMA's red warnings for Lisbon were unchanged at our last read of the timeline.
An earlier Lusa piece (CNN Portugal, 20:07) on the several possible entry points of the storm is about the uncertainty, not the shift, and is outside this table (items from 21:00).

Correction (00:50 UTC, 11 November): our first version of this table had RTP's 22:22 bulletin first and Observador at 23:16. We had not found Observador's live blog (its address names another story). With its entries read, Observador is first at 22:07 on the models and at 22:35 on IPMA's word; the order of the two on IPMA's word depends on what Antena 1's 22:00 bulletin said, which we did not hear.

Público: an article first published at 11:38 on 10 November (its address is about flooded roads) now carries the headline "Depressão Charles passa mais a sul do que o previsto e vento deverá ser menos intenso". The page gives its first publication time, not when the headline changed, so it cannot be placed in this table; it is the Público headline incident.conductor@ read at 00:29.

facts.what: IPMA names the storm Charles (communiqué no. 1)
facts.primary_note: IPMA's special communiqué no. 1, 9 November 13:17 (the timeline's row; data/weather/communiques.json)
facts.pattern: d[áa] nome|nome [àa] depress|depress[aã]o charles|tempestade charles|storm charles|bruna e charles
notes: Our read of 9 November is thin: feeds scroll, and our first read was at 23:45 on 10 November. An outlet missing here may simply have scrolled out.

facts.primary_note: ANEPC's Aviso 21, 9 November 20:30 (the timeline's row, read on prociv.gov.pt)
notes: Our read of 9 November is thin (see fact 8).

facts.what: The minister announces that schools and non-essential public services close on Wednesday (spoken, before the government's page)
facts.primary_note: no timed primary source for the spoken announcement: the reference is the earliest report we read (Diário de Notícias' live blog, 09:14:29). The government's page is dated 12:10 (fact 2)
facts.pattern: escolas e servi[cç]os p[úu]blicos|situa[cç][aã]o de alerta|closes schools|escolas(?! (na|da) madeira)[^:]*(encerrad|fecha)[^:]*quarta|declara[^.]{0,30}situa

facts.what: IPMA's meteorologist: the storm should enter between the Lisbon region and Cabo de São Vicente
facts.primary_note: a spoken statement to Rádio Observador; the reference is the earliest text we read (Observador's live blog, 22:35:24). IPMA's own channels had not changed at 00:29 on 11 November (fact 7)
facts.pattern: trajec?t[óo]ria|mais (a|para) sul|a sul de lisboa|further south|cabo de s[aã]o vicente|menos (vento|intens)

lag_rule: minutes_after_primary = whole minutes elapsed, truncated toward zero (19:09:00 to 19:41:31 is 32 minutes, not 33); seconds_after_primary carries the exact difference. Times are each page's own, to the second where the page gives seconds.
shape_for_other_series: To put another series (for example Wikipedia's first edit per fact) on the same axis: for each fact id here, a row {fact, series (e.g. "wikipedia-pt"), at (UTC), title or summary, url, via, seconds_after_primary, minutes_after_primary}. first-on-each-fact.json's facts[].first_by_outlet[] rows have that shape with `outlet` as the series and `published` as `at`.
